whatItFakes: Fresh generated public, institution, nonbusiness and unknown owners open with modeled zero-funded prototype journal cash pending genuine dated funding. The technical zero is not an observed zero balance and has no private-business calibration.
why: The superseded six-month payroll stock has no observed institutional balance, dated appropriation or funding receipt. Private JPMC employer/nonemployer cash evidence cannot supply those missing public or other unsupported owner facts.
replacement: REVIEW16 public-budget and national modules must supply genuine dated funding authority, appropriations and treasury/account receipts for represented institutions; other unsupported owners need separately source-qualified recorded funding. Preserve actual supplied balances. Never infer a measured zero, private JPMC reserve, survival stock or synthetic owner contribution.

whatItFakes: Carries a genuinely observed active 2017 county identity forward to the opening date using its official stable GID/PID alias and an already existing canonical county account. Intermediate identity-change history and actual opening active status remain unobserved.
why: The 2017 Census government listing was recorded before the January 1, 2021 opening; a later canonical directory cannot be backdated. Historical identity supplies an owner candidate, not legal powers, enacted appropriation or opening cash.
replacement: A dated opening government directory or independently sourced legal identity/change history matched to the same official government ID. Preserve the original 2017 observation date and account ID.

whatItFakes: Uses existing generated person countyIds and the observed 2020 county-to-place relation to qualify the represented share of a bounded opening purchase plan. Recorded geography and residency do not observe public demand, appropriation, custodial supplier reach, travel or delivery.
why: The county keeps its county jurisdiction while the represented cohort lives in a CDP. Census geography was observed April 1, 2020 but published August 12, 2021, so an earlier opening uses it only as a retrospective generation prior. Unverified membership remains unbound.
replacement: Dated own-county procurement/service-area records and actual contract scope with matched represented-resident coverage. A verified geographic relation alone must not close the existing public-procurement appropriation/price stopgap.

whatItFakes: Fresh employer-owned payroll frequency/phase/lag calendars estimated from dated business-frequency evidence and separately qualified public/education examples; no actual fictional employer term or legal compliance claimed.
why: Current owned work has attendance timetables and hourly wage proxies but no historical paycheck calendar. BLS business shares do not identify employer phase/lag, current headcount, government/education weights or payroll-group membership. Farm/unknown extrapolation, no-adjustment holidays and model boundaries remain unmeasured.
replacement: Qualified employer-owned dated compensation/payroll records and government/education policy calendars, actual legal-frequency/holiday/lag treatment, shared household payday source links and empirical startup cohort checks. Public-budget/national modules own actual government funding, not this timing prior.

whatItFakes: On a minimum wage's effective date the laws module replaces each underpaid work commitment's hourly rate directly in core work state.
why: core2 has no pay-change path: admitWorkCommitment is the only writer and no API ends or re-rates a commitment.
replacement: OPUS-CORE's work pay-change API (re-rate a commitment from a date with its source), called here instead.
resolution: Replaced by OPUS-CORE's rerateJob (core2-api-v12) in laws.ts raiseOne and raiseToFloor; counted residents' jobs rise too.

whatItFakes: A state or federal officeholder outside the town is a stable identity (name, gender, birth date, party) with no core2 person behind it.
why: core2 has no fill-in yet: a named person outside the town can't become a full person when clicked.
replacement: CORE's two-level fill-in builds the full person from this identity (seeded from the world and the seat), with kin and a past from PEOPLE.

whatItFakes: The end of each term in progress at the opening: seats staggered evenly across the office's term, ending January 1 after a regular election year.
why: Real election calendars and term-start dates for each office are M2's filing and election work.
replacement: Each office's real election dates and term-start rules (M2-02), read from data.

whatItFakes: On a special election's date the seat goes to the best-suited eligible person instead of the voters' choice.
why: M2's election engine hasn't been built on core2 yet.
replacement: The M2 election engine runs the special election and seats its winner.

whatItFakes: Every adult resident counts as a registered voter where filing or signing requires registration.
why: core2 has no voter registration record yet.
replacement: A registration record per person (registered, where, party where a state records it), written when people register; filing and signing read it.

whatItFakes: A stranger asked to sign a petition signs when their own sociability outweighs their wariness of conflict, instead of weighing the candidate's platform.
why: PEOPLE's views engine isn't on core2 yet, so a signer can't compare the platform with their own views.
replacement: The signer weighs the stated platform against their own views (PEOPLE's views engine), plus what they know of the candidate.

whatItFakes: Each person's political lean is their House district's 2024 vote moved by three personality facets, and their stance on a policy question is that lean along the question's measured left-right axis.
why: OPUS-PEOPLE's views engine (values and stances formed from each person's life) isn't on core2 yet.
replacement: Each person's own stances from PEOPLE's views engine, read through the same platformAgreement call.

whatItFakes: An ad reaches the adults with the fewest work hours, as a stand-in for who watches and scrolls most; ad time is bought from a stand-in local media seller.
why: People's media habits and the news outlets aren't modeled on core2 yet.
replacement: Each person's media habits and real outlets (PEOPLE and the news engine); ads bought from those outlets.

whatItFakes: Voters the world doesn't name vote as lean bands around the place's lean, sized from the district's 2024 votes (state and federal races) or the town's population times the 2024 share of people who voted (local races), each band voting with its named people.
why: CORE's voter groups exist as a table but generated worlds don't populate them yet.
replacement: CORE's populated voter groups (counts by place, age, job and household, with lean and turnout), each voting as a group.

whatItFakes: When filing closes, the incumbent stands again if alive, and each state or federal race gets a named challenger from the other major party.
why: OPUS-PEOPLE's 'who runs' (M2-04) isn't built: people deciding to run from their drives, views and circumstances.
replacement: PEOPLE's who-runs decisions file each candidate through fileCandidacy with recorded reasons; incumbents decide the same way.

whatItFakes: Counties and cities start their fiscal year on their state's date.
why: City and county fiscal calendars aren't researched yet (M1-budgets-taxes research item 1).
replacement: Each county's and city's own fiscal year start and adoption deadline, from charters and budget documents, with estimates for the rest.

whatItFakes: Local spending is shared between county and city by function (counties: welfare, health and hospitals, corrections, highways, natural resources; cities and townships: the rest), and local revenue in the same proportion.
why: Census reports local government finances combined, not by government.
replacement: Census FY2024 individual government finances (data/source/government-finances) for each county and city, with estimates for the rest.

whatItFakes: Each new fiscal year's budget is adopted on its start date by carrying the year's amounts forward.
why: Councils and legislatures can't vote budgets until M3 (owner, Oct 10: old budget rules until councils vote).
replacement: The council's or legislature's budget vote (M3-05) and the executive's priorities.

whatItFakes: A mayor's veto is overridden by two thirds of the members voting; ordinances take effect 30 days after enactment.
why: Each city's charter sets its own override majority and effective date; they aren't read yet.
replacement: Override majorities and ordinance effective dates from each state's municipal code and sampled charters, with estimates for the rest.

whatItFakes: Bodies over nine members refer bills to one subject committee of their most senior members (about a seventh of the body), chaired by the most senior member of the majority side; smaller bodies act as a committee of the whole.
why: Each body's committee rules, sizes, assignments and chairs aren't read yet.
replacement: Each council's, legislature's and Congress's committee rules and rosters (assignments earned through relationships and seniority, owner's M3 spec) from their own rules and sites.

whatItFakes: On a statewide ballot measure, the voters the world doesn't name vote as even lean bands around the state's 2024 presidential lean, sized by the state's 2024 vote, each band voting its own view of the question (no separate public-opinion level for the policy).
why: CORE's voter groups aren't populated in generated worlds, and OPUS-PEOPLE's views engine (with issue opinion beyond left-right) isn't built.
replacement: CORE's populated voter groups across the state, each voting from PEOPLE's views of the question.

whatItFakes: A recall petition's signatures from the town's unnamed voters are the named residents' signing share times the town's estimated electorate (population times the 2024 voting share), against whatever signature base the state's rule names.
why: CORE's voter groups and real voter rolls aren't populated in generated worlds.
replacement: Signatures gathered by the organizer's and volunteers' real contacts, plus CORE's voter groups, counted against the rule's own base (registered voters or last vote cast).

whatItFakes: An employers' group's lobbyist is the best-paid town resident working for the member business the bill costs most; businesses themselves decide to join and pay dues.
why: Businesses have no owners or managers in core2 yet (OPUS-WORLD's business engine), and lobbyists aren't a hired job yet.
replacement: The business owners decide to join, and the group hires a lobbyist (a person with a job, a record and memory of each member's votes).

whatItFakes: A hired staffer takes the post without a pay commitment: no wage flows from the government's treasury to them, and they keep any job they had.
why: Public payroll from government treasuries isn't wired in core2 yet (requested from OPUS-CORE).
replacement: A work commitment at the post's pay, paid from the government's treasury through the journal, ending any job the staffer leaves for it.

whatItFakes: A race the town doesn't vote in is decided by the seat's whole electorate at once: its 2024 lean (House district or state presidential vote; a state legislative district without a read result leans to its holder's party at the typical margin), the midterm environment and incumbency; candidates are a party, not people with records.
why: District-level voter groups and fictional candidates with records for every seat in the country aren't built (CORE voter groups; PEOPLE's who runs).
replacement: Each race run on the election engine with fictional candidates who have records and campaigns, and voter groups by district.

whatItFakes: States other than the town's vote for president by their 2024 lean plus one tunable shift against the party holding the presidency; Maine's and Nebraska's district electors go with the statewide winner; nominees are a party's fictional candidate without a primary season.
why: The national economy (OPUS-WORLD), the president's record and the primary calendar don't feed the race yet.
replacement: Each state's vote from its voter groups reacting to the economy, the record and the campaigns; nominees from state-by-state primaries; district electors in Maine and Nebraska.

whatItFakes: The wider population's purchases are merged per seller, kind and week of the month and paid monthly instead of after each household's own paydays; count workers always work their full schedule and are paid on the employer's cadence (semimonthly approximated as two monthly dates).
why: Two-level population (owner, Oct 11): only the circle is simulated person by person; the merged flows keep every monthly total equal to the full opening.
replacement: Wider-population spending timed from the counts' pay dates and income, with absence and turnover rates by industry checked against BLS JOLTS and CPS.

whatItFakes: A person filled in from the wider population keeps receiving their retirement income through the residents account; their cash share is their opening share of the residents' current cash, and their job's calendar copies the employer's cadence from the fill-in date.
why: Fill-in v2 moves cash, scheduled work and household purchases onto the person's own records; retirement income is tied to per-person award records funded through the outside payer's single obligation.
replacement: Done Oct 12: a filled-in retiree is paid their own award by the same outside payer on the same dates (the pooled retirement flow shrinks by exactly that amount). The cash share is an estimate from opening shares, and the job's calendar follows the employer's cadence, both by design.

whatItFakes: Buyers outside the town are one account per place paying each firm a fixed weekly share of its projected receipts (adjusted with its demand), not individual outside customers, freight orders, Medicaid claims or guests.
why: 11 of 14 closures in the first money year were firms with no customer route at all (owner order M0-money-fix); the share of receipts from outside the town is researched per industry.
replacement: Outside demand from the national and regional economy engines (OPUS-WORLD): exports, government programs and visitors as their own dated buyers.

whatItFakes: Each firm pays cash above twice its industry's median buffer to owners monthly, a fixed tunable share to the town's residents and the rest outside; no firm has recorded owners, retained-earnings policy, taxes or investment.
why: Without payouts, firms kept every dollar of profit and residents ran out of cash within the year (Mill Creek, Oklahoma: firms +$77M, residents $7.7M to $0).
replacement: OPUS-WORLD's business engine: recorded owners (local people or outside), payout and investment decisions from the firm's own conditions, and business taxes.

whatItFakes: Counted residents the opening couldn't place in a town firm (the employment target from ACS/CPS less recorded jobs) earn the town's median recorded wage, paid every two weeks from outside, without employers, commutes or industries.
why: The opening's town workplaces cover only part of the county's industry mix (e.g. 34% in Mill Creek, Oklahoma), so most working residents had no income and the residents' account ran dry within months.
replacement: Recorded jobs for every employed resident: town firms in the missing industries (health care, education, government) and commutes to employers in other places (LEHD LODES origin-destination flows), with their own pay.

whatItFakes: A business closed by its owner's choice ends its jobs the same day without a final paycheck for wages earned since the last payday, and without paying off open supplier or credit balances; the owner takes all remaining cash.
why: WORLD's owners needed a way to close a solvent business; a full wind-down (final pay, settling payables, selling assets) is not built yet.
replacement: A wind-down that settles earned wages and open balances from the business's cash before the owner's distribution.

whatItFakes: Each household's assigned living cost (CEX basket plus HUD Fair Market Rent) not bought from a recorded local seller is paid to one outside account on the 1st: no landlord, mortgage, utility or outside store.
why: Rent and non-local spending were never paid, so household cash grew without limit.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD's housing engine (rent and mortgages to owners and lenders) and outside-spending model (category location-quotient leakage); turn this off with collapseToTwoLevels(input, { outsideLivingCosts: false }).

whatItFakes: A named person filled in from a recorded identity (e.g. a state or federal official) gets neutral traits, no family or acquaintances, no cash and a monthly cadence.
why: Traits, kin and past come from the opening's generation world, which a running core doesn't have; GOV needs full officials now (SG-GOV-official-identity-only).
replacement: PEOPLE's trait, kin and past builders seeded from the world seed and the identity (as fill-in of counted residents does), and the official's pay from the public payroll.

whatItFakes: Counted adults vote as one group per place and age band: every counted adult is treated as an eligible citizen, turnout is the state's CPS 2024 rate for the age band (national where no state row exists), and every group starts with the state's 2024 presidential two-party margin as its lean.
why: In a two-level town only about 60 named people vote individually; elections need the counted population to vote from its own records (PLAY's report on GOV's elections).
replacement: Groups split by citizenship (ACS), place-level 2024 results and residents' own views (PEOPLE's views engine) and refined by GOV's elections.

whatItFakes: Paid family leave collects its payroll premium but pays no leave: nobody claims leave for a birth, adoption or a relative's illness.
why: There is no birth-leave or caregiving event a worker can claim leave from, and no benefit payment route from a treasury to a person.
replacement: PEOPLE: a leave-taking choice on a birth or a relative's serious illness (health engine), and CORE: a benefit payment from a government treasury to a person through the journal (e.g. payBenefit(treasuryId, personId, amountMinor, source)); then GOV pays wage replacement from the premium fund.

whatItFakes: Public-sector collective bargaining records the right on public workers, their employers and the union, but no contract is bargained and no pay changes.
why: There is no bargaining engine: no union contract, no bargaining unit wage or table.
replacement: GOV: a bargaining engine that negotiates the unit's contract with the public employer and applies it with CORE's rerateJob(jobId, hourlyMinor, source); WORLD: union membership on workers' records.

whatItFakes: Right-to-work records the right on workers and the rule on the union, but no union dues or agency fees exist to stop.
why: Workers' union membership and dues aren't modeled.
replacement: WORLD or CORE: union membership on jobs and dues as a payroll deduction through the journal (e.g. a standing dues contract per member), which right-to-work then ends for nonmembers.

whatItFakes: Legal cannabis sales record eligibility on adults 21 and over and on retailers, but no cannabis is sold.
why: Household purchases have no cannabis category and no licensed retailer enters the market.
replacement: WORLD: a household purchase kind for cannabis (CES-based) and a licensed retailer entering through CORE's enterMarket({organizationId, financeKinds: [household.cannabis], ...}).

whatItFakes: The consumer loan rate cap records the right on adults, but no person holds a loan to reprice.
why: Credit facilities exist only for organizations; people have no consumer loans.
replacement: CORE: consumer credit for people (credit facilities with a person borrower); then GOV reprices loans above the cap with CORE's repriceCreditFacility(facilityId, cap, source).

whatItFakes: Allowing multifamily homes records the right on builders and the counted residents, but no homes get built.
why: There is no housing stock or construction engine.
replacement: WORLD: a housing engine with lots, units and construction decisions (e.g. addHousingCapacity(placeId, units) driven by builders' returns).

whatItFakes: Housing spending records rent help on the lowest-cash households the extra money covers, but no rent payment is made for them.
why: Households have no rent contracts to pay toward.
replacement: WORLD: rent contracts on renting households; CORE: a benefit payment from a treasury toward a household's rent through the journal.

whatItFakes: The inclusionary requirement records the duty on builders, but no affordable units are set aside.
why: There is no housing construction to apply a set-aside to.
replacement: WORLD: the housing engine's new units, with the set-aside share priced below market for eligible households.

whatItFakes: Rent stabilization records the cap on adults and landlords, but no rent is capped because tenure and rents aren't recorded.
why: Households have no tenure (renter or owner) or rent contract; living costs carry a HUD shelter budget only.
replacement: WORLD: household tenure and rent contracts; then GOV caps increases with CORE's setStandingContractAmount(contractId, amountMinor).

whatItFakes: The right to counsel records the right on residents and the duty on the city, but no eviction case is ever heard.
why: There are no eviction filings or courts.
replacement: WORLD and GOV: eviction filings from unpaid rent contracts and a housing court; the city's legal services pay for counsel through the journal.

whatItFakes: Partnering with immigration enforcement reaches an estimated count of noncitizen adults (national share) instead of named noncitizens.
why: People have no citizenship record.
replacement: PEOPLE: citizenship and immigration status on people and counted residents (ACS B05001 by place); then the policy reaches the named people it covers.

whatItFakes: Ending cash bail records the right on adults and an estimated count of people held before trial, but nobody is arrested or held.
why: There is no arrest, charge or jail engine.
replacement: GOV: a justice engine with arrests, charges, pretrial detention and release decisions from the law in force.

whatItFakes: Felony disenfranchisement uses the national share of the voting-age population (and the share restored) instead of people's own records.
why: People have no conviction or sentence records.
replacement: GOV and PEOPLE: conviction and sentence records on people and counted residents; voting eligibility then reads each record.

whatItFakes: Child access prevention records the storage duty on every adult in a household with a child, not only gun owners.
why: Gun ownership isn't recorded.
replacement: PEOPLE: firearm ownership on households (from survey rates by state, seeded per household at generation).

whatItFakes: Independent redistricting records the rule on legislators, but no district lines are drawn by anyone.
why: There is no redistricting engine.
replacement: GOV: a redistricting step after each census that draws districts, run by the commission when this law is in force.

whatItFakes: For an island area the budgets module records no residents, group B shares a budget line's change to the town by the Census population in its own parameter table.
why: data/research/money/public-budget-bases.json has no population2024 (and no budget) for Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa or the Northern Mariana Islands.
replacement: OPUS-GOV budgets: public-budget-bases.json carries each island area's population and finances (Census Island Areas, PR government finances); group B then reads GovernmentRow.residents only.

whatItFakes: Where the town has no public school employer, teachers and staff at the town's private school stand in for public school staff: a teacher-salary floor and a schools budget line reach them.
why: The core opening never imports the town's public schools as an employer (no service:school jobs in generated worlds), so a public-school pay law has no one to reach.
replacement: OPUS-CORE imports the town's public school district as a service:school employer with its staff (NCES district and CCD staff counts); the stand-in is dropped and only public school jobs are covered.

whatItFakes: Fare-free transit and the transit budget line are records on riders (fare 0, service level) and a transit budget line; no rider pays or saves a fare.
why: No transit trips or fares exist in the core: households have no commute purchases.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD prices API: setPlacePrice({ placeId, good: "transit-fare", priceMinor, source }) read by household commuting costs, so riders' costs fall to zero and the line pays the transit operator.

whatItFakes: A mileage fee replacing the fuel tax is a price record (cents a mile) on drivers; no driver pays it.
why: No vehicle miles, fuel purchases or fuel tax exist in the core.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD prices API: setPlaceTax({ placeId, good: "vehicle-miles", centsPerUnit, payeeAccountId }) on household fuel and travel spending, with the fuel tax removed.

whatItFakes: Public broadband is an offer record (monthly price) on household heads and a competitor record on telecom firms; no household switches or pays.
why: Household utility bills are not modeled as contracts a law can change.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD household bills API: offerHouseholdService({ placeId, service: "broadband", providerId, monthlyMinor }) so households can take the public offer and telecom revenue moves.

whatItFakes: Medicaid expansion and its work requirement are eligibility records on named adults and counted shares; no one's health coverage or medical costs change.
why: The core has no health coverage or medical spending for people.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE health engine: setCoverage(personId, { plan: "medicaid", from, to }) and counted-group coverage shares, read by medical costs (OPUS-CORE household spending).

whatItFakes: An assistance work requirement is a time-limit record on named adults and counted shares; no SNAP benefit is paid or cut.
why: The core pays no SNAP or other means-tested benefits to households.
replacement: OPUS-CORE benefits API: addBenefit({ personId|householdId, program: "snap", monthlyMinor, from, payerAccountId }) and endBenefit(id), which this time limit ends after three months.

whatItFakes: Universal preschool is an eligibility record on named 3- and 4-year-olds and a counted share; no child enrolls and no family's child-care cost changes.
why: There is no school enrollment or child-care spending in the core.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE schools engine: enroll(childId, schoolOrgId, { program: "pre-k" }) and OPUS-CORE household child-care cost, reduced when enrolled.

whatItFakes: Public funds for private schooling are an eligibility record (amount) on named school-age children and a record on private schools; no voucher is paid.
why: No child is enrolled at a school, so a payment can't follow a student.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE schools engine: enrollment(childId) naming the school; then the voucher pays from the treasury to the private school through accounts.transfer each term.

whatItFakes: A property-tax growth cap is a right record (cap share) on household heads; no property tax bill exists to cap.
why: Households pay no property tax in the core; the budgets module records property tax only as a revenue line.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD housing engine: property tax bills on owners (assessed value times the rate in force) with an assessment-growth cap read from the law in force.

whatItFakes: Sales tax rates and a grocery exemption are price records on household heads and retailers; purchases collect no sales tax for any treasury.
why: Household purchase flows (finance contracts, the residents purchase flows) have no tax line.
replacement: OPUS-CORE purchase API: setPurchaseTax({ placeId, category: "all"|"groceries", ratePercent, payeeAccountId }) applied to each household purchase and remitted to the treasury.

whatItFakes: A ban on new gas hookups is a compliance record on builders and utilities; no building cost or fuel choice changes.
why: No construction projects or building fuel choices exist in the core.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD housing and business engine: new-construction cost and appliance fuel by code in force (setBuildingCode({ placeId, allElectric: true })).

whatItFakes: A clean electricity standard and a carbon price are price records (share or dollars a ton) on household heads and compliance records on utilities and emitters; no price or bill changes.
why: Household energy bills and business energy costs aren't modeled as prices a law can move.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD prices API: adjustPrice({ placeId, good: "electricity"|"fuel", share, cause }) read by household and business costs.

whatItFakes: A bottle deposit is a compliance record on sellers (deposit per container); no deposit is charged or refunded.
why: Retail purchases carry no per-container charge.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD prices API: addPerUnitCharge({ placeId, good: "beverage-container", centsPerUnit, refundable: true }).

whatItFakes: A clean air plan binds the town's industrial employers (compliance record) wherever it's law, whether or not the county is in nonattainment.
why: No EPA Green Book nonattainment list is loaded for counties.
replacement: Load EPA Green Book nonattainment counties as data; the plan then binds emitters only in listed counties, and OPUS-WORLD business costs read the compliance record.

whatItFakes: Groundwater limits and the natural resources line are compliance and service records on farms, mines and utilities; no output or cost changes.
why: Business production costs don't read regulations or resource limits.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD business engine: setOperatingLimit({ organizationId, input: "groundwater", share }) and regulatory cost read by business books.

whatItFakes: Farmland protection is a rule record on farms, builders and real-estate firms; no parcel or development changes.
why: Land parcels and development aren't modeled.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD housing engine: land parcels with zoning, read by new construction (zoneParcels({ placeId, use: "agricultural", protected: true })).

whatItFakes: The highways line is a road service level record on drivers and road builders; commute time and vehicle costs don't change.
why: There is no road condition or commuting cost in the core.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD regional engine: setRoadCondition({ placeId, level }) read by commute time and vehicle costs.

whatItFakes: The higher education line is a support level record on 18-to-24-year-olds; no tuition is charged or changed.
why: No college enrollment or tuition exists in the core.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE schools engine: college enrollment and tuition (setTuition({ institutionId, inStateMinor })) read by household spending.

whatItFakes: The parks line is a service level record on residents and recreation firms; no one's time use or well-being changes.
why: People's leisure doesn't read park service levels.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE time-use and needs: park service level read by leisure choices and well-being (placeService({ placeId, service: "parks", level })).

whatItFakes: Where the state's law settles an exact election tie by lot (about 34 states for general elections, 51 for primaries), the game holds a second election between the tied candidates instead.
why: A lot is a random draw, and the owner's no-dice rule bars a seeded draw from deciding an outcome; the owner hasn't ruled on legally required lots.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either a lot drawn as the law requires (a visible procedure, recorded), or keep the second election.

whatItFakes: A local outlet's record name is its kind (newspaper, television, radio); outlets are sized from state counts, not named real outlets.
why: Outlet names are player text and come from the English engine; the per-place outlet roster isn't researched.
replacement: Names from the English engine (OPUS-PEOPLE) and per-county outlet rosters from Medill and FCC data.
